facts.c: A labour contract can be written or verbal; if it needs registering, this is free
facts.q: It can be written or verbal. It can be drawn up and signed according to local custom. If it needs registering, this shall be done at no cost.

facts.c: A fixed-duration contract can last at most two years including renewals; breaking this rule turns it into an unlimited-duration contract
facts.q: The labor contract signed with consent for a specific duration cannot be for a period longer than two years. It can be renewed one or more times, as long as the renewal does not surpass the maximum duration of two years. Any violation of this rule leads the contract to become a labor contract of undetermined duration.

facts.c: A fixed-duration contract must be in writing, or it becomes an unlimited-duration contract
facts.q: A contract of a fixed duration must be in writing. If not, it becomes a labor contract of undetermined duration.

facts.c: Probation may last at most 3 months for regular employees, 2 months for specialised workers and 1 month for non-specialised workers
facts.q: the probationary period cannot last longer than three months for regular employees, two months for specialized workers and one month for non-specialized workers.

facts.c: A fixed-duration contract can be ended early only by written agreement of both sides in the presence of a Labour Inspector, or for serious misconduct or an act of God
facts.q: It can, however, be terminated before the ending date if both parties are in agreement on the condition that this agreement is made in form of writing in the presence of a Labor Inspector and signed by the two parties to the contract.

facts.c: If the employer alone ends a fixed-duration contract early (no serious misconduct or act of God), the worker gets damages at least equal to the pay until the contract's end
facts.q: entitles the worker to damages in an amount at least equal to the remuneration he would have received until the termination of the contract.

facts.c: If the worker alone ends a fixed-duration contract early without valid reason, the employer is entitled to damages for the harm suffered
facts.q: The premature termination of the contract by the will of the worker alone for reasons other than those mentioned in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this article entitles the employer to damages in an amount that corresponds to the damage sustained.

facts.c: For a fixed-duration contract over 6 months, the worker must be told of non-renewal 10 days ahead (15 days if over 1 year); without notice the contract is extended
facts.q: If the contract has a duration of more than six months, the worker must be informed of the expiration of the contract or of its non-renewal ten days in advance. This notice period is extended to fifteen days for contracts that have a duration of more than one year.

facts.c: At the end of any contract the worker can ask the employer for an employment certificate
facts.q: In every case of contract termination, the worker can require the employer to provide him with an employment certificate.

facts.c: Notice periods for ending an unlimited-duration contract: 7 days (under 6 months' service), 15 days (6 months to 2 years), 1 month (2 to 5 years), 2 months (5 to 10 years), 3 months (over 10 years)
facts.q: Seven days, if the worker's length of continuous service is less than six months; Fifteen days, if the worker's length of continuous service is from six months to two years; One month, if the worker's length of continuous service is longer then two years and up to five years.

facts.c: Dismissal without proper notice obliges the employer to pay wages and benefits for the notice period
facts.q: entails the obligation of the employer to compensate the worker the amount equal to the wages and all kinds of benefits that the worker would have received during the official notice period.

facts.c: No dismissal without a valid reason related to the worker's aptitude or behaviour or the enterprise's operational needs
facts.q: However, no layoff can be taken without a valid reason relating to the worker's aptitude or behavior, based on the requirements of the operation of the enterprise, establishment or group.

facts.c: During the notice period the worker gets two paid days off a week to look for a new job
facts.q: During the notice period, the worker of the enterprise is entitled to two days leave per week with full payment to look for a new job.

facts.c: Serious offences by the employer include fraud to get a worker to sign, refusing to pay all or part of wages, repeated late pay, abuse, threats or violence
facts.q: 1. The use of fraudulent measures to entice a worker into signing a contract under conditions to which he would not otherwise have agreed, if he had realized it; 2. Refusal to pay all or part of the wages; 3. Repeated late payment of wages; 4. Abusive language, threat, violence or assault;

facts.c: No notice is needed when one party commits a serious offence
facts.q: 2. For a serious offense on the part of one of the parties.

facts.c: Serious offences by the worker include theft, presenting false documents at signing, and threats or assault
facts.q: Fraudulent acts committed at the time of signing (presentation of false documentation)

facts.c: If the employer's unfair treatment or repeated contract breaches push the worker to quit, the worker can still claim indemnity and damages
facts.q: If the employer treats the worker unfairly or repeatedly violates the terms of the contract, he also has to pay indemnities and damages to the worker.

facts.c: Bankruptcy and closure of the business do not release the employer from its termination obligations
facts.q: Bankruptcy and judicial liquidation are not considered as acts of God.

facts.c: Refusing to give an employment certificate obliges the employer to pay damages
facts.q: The refusal to supply this certificate obliges the employer to pay damages to the worker.

facts.c: Wages must be paid directly to the worker, in legal currency
facts.q: The wage must be paid directly to the worker concerned, unless the worker agrees to get paid through other methods.

facts.c: The employer may not restrict how the worker uses his wage
facts.q: The employer, however, is prohibited from restricting the worker's freedom to using his wage at his disposal.

facts.c: When a contract ends, wages and any indemnity must be paid within 48 hours
facts.q: In the event of termination of a labor contract, wage and indemnity of any kind must be paid within forty-eight hours following the date of termination of work.

facts.c: In a wage dispute the employer must prove payment, through the worker's signature (or two witnesses' if illiterate) in the payroll ledger
facts.q: In the event of disputes over the payment of wages, the employer has the duty to prove that he has made the payment.

facts.c: Signing that 'all wages are paid' or accepting pay without protest does not give up the right to unpaid wages
facts.q: Even though the worker accepts payment without protest, this does not mean that he has renounced the right to payment of all or part of his wages

facts.c: A wage claim lapses three years after the wage was due
facts.q: A lapse of a lawsuit for the payment of wages is three years from the date the wage was due.

facts.c: Deducting from wages for job placement, for the employer, its representative or a labour recruiter, is prohibited
facts.q: Wage deductions for the purpose of job placement that are provided directly or indirectly to an employer, to his representative, or to any intermediary such as a labor recruiter are prohibited.

facts.c: Employer deductions are limited to unreturned tools, items in the worker's care, advances for them and company-store debts, and may never take more than the worker needs to live
facts.q: However, the total amount deducted from the wage, in any case, cannot surpass the portion deemed necessary to provide the basic living for the worker and his family.

facts.c: Normal hours may not exceed 8 a day or 48 a week
facts.q: the number of hours worked by workers of either sex cannot exceed eight hours per day, or 48 hours per week.

facts.c: No worker may be used more than six days a week; weekly rest is at least 24 consecutive hours, in principle on Sunday
facts.q: Weekly time off shall last for a minimum of twenty-four consecutive hours. All workers shall be given in principle a day off on Sunday.

facts.c: Paid annual leave is 1.5 working days per month of continuous service, plus one day per three years of service
facts.q: at the rate of one and a half work days of paid leave per month of continuous service.

facts.c: Annual leave increases by one day for every three years of service
facts.q: The length of paid leave as stated above is increased according to the seniority of workers at the rate of one day per three years of service.

facts.c: The right to take paid leave comes after one year; a contract ending earlier earns pay in place of the leave
facts.q: The right to use paid leave is acquired after one year of service.

facts.c: If the contract ends before leave is taken, the worker gets an indemnity for the leave earned
facts.q: If the contract is terminated or expires before the worker has acquired the right to use his paid-leave, an indemnity calculated on the basis of Article 166 above is granted to the worker.

facts.c: Women get 90 days' maternity leave and cannot be dismissed during it
facts.q: In all enterprises covered by Article 1 of this law, women shall be entitled to a maternity leave of ninety days.

facts.c: Maternity leave pays half wages from the employer, only for women with at least one year's service
facts.q: However, the wage benefits specified in the first paragraph of this article shall be granted only to women having a minimum of one year of uninterrupted service in the enterprise.

facts.c: Forced labour and work to pay off debts are forbidden
facts.q: Hiring of people for work to pay off debts is forbidden.

facts.c: Absence for illness certified by a doctor suspends the contract for up to six months
facts.q: The absence of the worker for illness certified by a qualified doctor. This absence is limited to six months

facts.c: No foreigner may work without a work permit and an employment card from the labour ministry
facts.q: No foreigner can work unless he possesses a work permit and an employment card issued by the Ministry in Charge of Labor.

facts.c: The work permit lasts one year and can be extended within the validity of the residence permit
facts.q: The work permit is valid for one year and may be extended as long as the validity of extension does not exceed the fixed period in the residency permit of the person in question.

facts.c: The labour ministry can revoke a work permit when the holder is unemployed for more than a month or is hired by another employer
facts.q: When the holder is unemployed for more than one month or is hired by another employer.

facts.c: An individual dispute can first go to the provincial or municipal Labour Inspector for conciliation
facts.q: Prior to any judicial action, an individual dispute can be referred for a preliminary conciliation, at the initiative of one of the parties, to the Labor Inspector of his province or municipality.

facts.c: An agreement reached before the Labour Inspector is legally enforceable; parties can be assisted or represented
facts.q: An agreement made before the Labor Inspector is enforceable by law.

facts.c: If conciliation fails, the party has two months to file in court, or the claim lapses
facts.q: In case of non-conciliation, the interested party can file a complaint in a court of competent jurisdiction within two months, otherwise the litigation will be lapsed.

facts.c: Hiring or keeping a foreigner without an employment card: fine of 61 to 90 days' base daily wage or 6 days to 1 month's jail for the employer
facts.q: Any person who hires or keeps in his service a foreigner, who does not possess the employment card authorizing him to carry out a paid job in the Kingdom of Cambodia, is liable to a fine of sixty-one to ninety days of the base daily wage or to imprisonment of six days to one month.

facts.c: Overtime is paid at 150% of normal pay, and 200% at night or on the weekly day off
facts.q: the overtime hours shall be paid at a rate of fifty percent higher than normal hours. If the overtime hours are worked at night or during weekly time off, the rate of increase shall be one hundred percent.

facts.c: From 1 January 2027 the minimum wage in textiles, garments, footwear, travel goods and bags is USD 212 a month for regular workers and USD 210 for probationers (Prakas 226/26 of 30 September 2026)
facts.q: Regular workers/employees: USD 212 per month

facts.c: Probationary garment-sector workers get at least USD 210 a month from 1 January 2027
facts.q: Probationary workers/employees: USD 210 per month

facts.c: Piece-rate workers whose output pay falls below the minimum must be topped up to it
facts.q: If their output-based earnings fall below the applicable minimum wage, the employer must pay the difference

facts.c: A temporary transport and accommodation allowance of USD 2.50 a month continues in 2027
facts.q: the temporary transportation and accommodation allowance of USD 2.50 per month, established by the decision dated 20 March 2026, will continue to apply in 2027.

facts.c: In 2026 the garment-sector minimum wage is USD 210 a month for regular workers and USD 208 for probationers (Prakas 214/25)
facts.q: for regular workers, USD 210 per month; and (2) for probationary workers, USD 208 per month.

facts.c: Garment-sector workers also get USD 7 a month transport or accommodation allowance, USD 10 attendance bonus, USD 0.5 a day meal allowance (or a free meal) for overtime, and a USD 2 to 11 seniority bonus
facts.q: such as compensation for a transportation or accommodation allowance of USD 7 per month, an attendance bonus of USD 10 per month, a meal allowance of USD 0.5 per day (or one free meal per day) for workers who work overtime and a seniority bonus from USD 2 to USD 11

facts.c: The statutory minimum wage covers only garment, textile, footwear, travel goods and bag manufacturing; other industries have none
facts.q: Yes, the minimum wage law currently applies only to the garment, textile, footwear, and travel goods sectors. Other industries are not subject to this mandated minimum wage.

facts.c: Since 2019, workers on unlimited-duration contracts get a seniority payment of 7.5 days' wages and benefits in June and 7.5 days in December (15 days a year), replacing the old dismissal indemnity
facts.q: 7.5 days of the employee’s wages and other fringe benefits, to be paid in June of each year; and

facts.c: Workers on fixed-duration contracts get no seniority payment but severance of 5% of the wages for the contract's length
facts.q: Employees hired under a specific duration contract (an employment contract with a fixed start and end date) will not receive the seniority payment, but are entitled to severance pay, calculated at 5% of the wages the employee would have received during the length of the contract

facts.c: Prakas 442 (2018) requires pay twice a month from January 2019: 50% in the second week and the rest plus benefits in the fourth week
facts.q: Must be made in the second week of the month and consist of 50% of the employee’s actual wages for the month

facts.c: A worker who resigns before the end of June or December loses that half-year's seniority payment; no seniority indemnity is due on resignation or dismissal for serious misconduct
facts.q: However, if the employee resigns before the end of June or December, he/she will not be eligible for the payment.

facts.c: The seniority payment is paid with the second wage payment of June and December
facts.q: The seniority indemnity will be paid together with wages in the second payment of June and December.

facts.c: The probation period does not count toward seniority
facts.q: The employment period begins after the employment agreement is signed and the employee is hired on a full-time basis, exclusive of any probation period.

facts.c: Under Prakas 112/25 (6 May 2025) overtime must be voluntary and cannot be forced through coercion or discipline
facts.q: However, the overtime work must be conducted voluntarily and must not be enforced through coercion or disciplinary action.

facts.c: Overtime may not take total hours over 10 a day except for disaster prevention or repair
facts.q: overtime must not cause total working hours to exceed 10 hours per day, except in cases of disaster prevention or rectification.

facts.c: Overtime pay: 150% in daytime on working days; 200% from 10 pm to 5 am and on weekly days off
facts.q: 150% or one-and-a-half times the normal wages for overtime work conducted during the daytime on regular working days; 200% or twice the normal wages for overtime work conducted from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. (overnight) and on weekly days off

facts.c: Work on paid public holidays is voluntary
facts.q: employees may be requested to perform work on paid public holidays on a voluntary basis.

facts.c: After night overtime the employer must provide accommodation or transport
facts.q: employers must provide appropriate accommodation or transportation to employees following nighttime overtime work.

facts.c: Employers must file overtime on MLVT's LACMS system at least three working days ahead, with a confirmation signed or thumbprinted by two-thirds of staff representatives or over half the workers involved
facts.q: A confirmation letter signed or thumbprinted by either two-thirds of the staff representatives or by over 50% of the total employees involved.

facts.c: Cambodia's 2026 paid public holidays (Anukret 167 and MLVT Prakas 216) include Khmer New Year 14-16 April, Pchum Ben 10-12 October and the Water Festival 23-25 November
facts.q: Khmer New Year

facts.c: Since the 2021 amendment of Article 162, a public holiday falling on a Sunday no longer gives a substitute day off
facts.q: Under the amended Article 162 of the Labour Law, workers no longer get a substitute day off when a public holiday falls on a Sunday.

facts.c: A full-time worker earns 18 working days of annual leave per 12 months
facts.q: This means 18 working days for 12 months of service.

facts.c: The Labour Law gives no paid sick leave; ministry policy is 100% pay in the first month, 60% in the second and third, unpaid from the fourth to sixth
facts.q: The Labour Law does not provide for paid sick leave; however, following the policy of the Ministry of Labour, employers may provide paid sick leave as follows: - 100% of wages during the first month of sick leave; - 60% of wages during the second & third months of sick leave; and - unpaid leave from the fourth to the sixth month.

facts.c: Instruction 015/25 requires the employer to pay the 50% maternity wages in full before leave starts; NSSF pays 70% for 90 days to women with 9 months' contributions in the last 12
facts.q: now requires employers to pay all due wages in full (i.e., 50%) before the worker starts her maternity leave.

facts.c: NSSF pays 70% of reference earnings for 90 days to a woman with 9 months' contributions in the last 12
facts.q: An employee who has 9 months of contribution in the last 12 months is granted 70% of the reference earnings for 90 days from Social Security (NSSF).

facts.c: Every enterprise with one or more workers must register with NSSF, and all paid workers, Cambodian and foreign, are covered
facts.q: All workers, both Cambodian and foreigner, are employed at the enterprise/establishment with wages.

facts.c: NSSF members get free care at health facilities with an NSSF agreement (NSSF logo)
facts.q: The NSSF member have entitlement to access medical care services free of charge at the health facility signed the agreement with NSSF.

facts.c: Absence for sickness, accident or maternity with a prescription over 7 consecutive days earns 70% of contributory wage from NSSF, up to 180 days in 12 months
facts.q: for over 7 (seven) consecutive days, he will receive 70% of his contributory wage from NSSF

facts.c: The daily allowance needs health-care contributions for 2 consecutive months or 6 months in the last 12
facts.q: Employer has paid contributions of Health Care for 2 consecutive months or at least 6 months within the last 12 months

facts.c: After a work injury, NSSF pays 70% of contributory wage from the second day until recovery; the employer pays the first day
facts.q: the victim concerned will receive 70% of his contributory wage starting from the second day of accident until recovery.

facts.c: A caretaker of an injured worker gets 50% of the worker's daily allowance
facts.q: a caretaker of victim will also receive 50% of victim's daily allowance for temporary disability.

facts.c: Permanent disability under 20% is paid as a lump sum; 20% or more as a monthly pension
facts.q: in case the victim has permanent disability from 20% up, NSSF provides monthly pension.

facts.c: If a work injury kills the worker, NSSF pays body transport and 4 million riels to whoever holds the funeral
facts.q: Provide 4 million riels to person who is responsible for holding the funeral.

facts.c: NSSF takes responsibility for corpse transportation cost after a fatal work injury
facts.q: Take responsibility for corpse transportation cost

facts.c: A surviving spouse gets a survivors' pension for life unless remarried; children until 18 (21 if studying)
facts.q: Spouse will receive Survivors' Pension for his/her whole life as long as she/he does not remarry.

facts.c: Survivors' benefit claims need a family record book, residence certificate, marriage certificate or copy
facts.q: Eligibility: All beneficiaries must have family record book, certificate of residency, marriage certificate, or a copy of marriage certificate.

facts.c: After a work injury the employer must inform NSSF at once on 1286 and send the work-injury form within 48 hours, directly or to benefit@nssf.gov.kh
facts.q: In case the worker has work injury, employer must inform NSSF immediately via 1286

facts.c: Work-injury forms go to NSSF directly or to benefit@nssf.gov.kh within 48 hours
facts.q: benefit@nssf.gov.kh in a qualifying period of 48 hours

facts.c: Claims for daily allowance and funeral grant after a work injury are valid for 1 year; permanent disability for 5 years
facts.q: Entitlement to daily allowance and funeral grant due to work injury is valid for 1 year, while entitlement to permanent disability benefits is valid for 5 years.

facts.c: Foreign workers attach their passport and NSSF card to benefit claims
facts.q: for the foreigner and the NSSF membership card of victim.

facts.c: If asked to pay at an NSSF facility, show the NSSF card and call 1286; in an emergency call 1286 for an ambulance
facts.q: If you are required to pay the service cost, please call 1286.

facts.c: NSSF pays benefit cheques: it calls the worker within 20 to 30 working days to collect the cheque
facts.q: NSSF will contact you through the given phone number within 20 to 30 working days at the latest in order to pick up the cheque

facts.c: NSSF keeps original documents; workers should keep copies
facts.q: Please make a copy of all documents and keep a set for yourself (worker) because NSSF requires all original copies in order to process claims.

facts.c: NSSF headquarters: Building 3, Russian Federation Blvd, Tuek Laak I, Toul Kork, Phnom Penh (MLVT compound); info@nssf.gov.kh; 1286
facts.q: Building 3, Russian Federation Blvd, Sangkat Tuek Laak I, Khan Toul Kork, Phnom Penh (in the compound of the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training).

facts.c: A worker who changes job stays covered for work injury only if the new employer registers him
facts.q: If worker changes job, he is still covered by Occupational Risk Scheme if his new employer registers him at NSSF.

facts.c: Employers must register workers with NSSF within 3 days of hiring, using the passport for foreign workers
facts.q: no later than 3 (three) days from the date of employment except workers/employees who have been registered.

facts.c: The NSSF membership card is free
facts.q: The NSSF membership card shall be provided free of charge.

facts.c: Pension contributions in the first 5 years are 4% of contributory wage: 2% employer, 2% worker
facts.q: 2% (two percent) shall be borne by workers/employees.

facts.c: The pension contribution rises to 8% for the five years after the first five
facts.q: Step 2: the contribution shall be set at 8% (eight percent) of the contributory wage

facts.c: The employer collects both shares and pays NSSF by the 15th of the next month
facts.q: Employers or owners of enterprises/establishments shall have an obligation to collect and pay contribution for pension scheme for their portion and workers/employees' portion to the account of the NSSF at any partner bank no later than the 15th (fifteenth) of the following month.

facts.c: The old-age pension needs age 60 and at least 12 months of contributions; with fewer, the member gets an old-age allowance (contributions paid, indexed)
facts.q: Be at least 60 (sixty) years of age and

facts.c: With under 12 months of contributions the member gets an old-age allowance equal to contributions paid adjusted by the price index
facts.q: In case NSSF members who are workers/employees fail to meet the conditions in Point 3 of Paragraph 1 above, they shall be entitled to old age allowance.

facts.c: The old-age allowance claim is due within 1 month after turning 60
facts.q: For NSSF members to be entitled to old age allowance shall fill out the old age allowance claim form within 1 (one) month after they have reached the age of 60 (sixty).

facts.c: NSSF said in 2022 that all foreign workers must join the pension scheme, which started on 1 October 2022, with benefits from 60 if residing in Cambodia
facts.q: has confirmed that all foreign workers must participate in the new co-payment pension fund scheme

facts.c: In 2022 a lump-sum withdrawal for foreign workers leaving for good was only under discussion
facts.q: the allowance for foreign workers to withdraw their money when deciding to leave Cambodia was not yet confirmed.

facts.c: Foreign workers are registered by passport number and fingerprints and must update a new passport at an NSSF office
facts.q: they must attend an NSSF office and using their biometric fingerprints register with their new passport number

facts.c: Foreign workers can check on the NSSF smartphone app that the employer pays contributions each month
facts.q: To verify you are properly registered under the NSSF foreign workers can download the NSSF application on their smartphones to ensure their employers are properly contributing to the scheme every month.

facts.c: Next of kin of a foreign worker who dies before 60 can receive the payout
facts.q: foreign employees under the scheme that die before the age of 60 can have their next–of–kin eligible to receive the payout.

facts.c: From November 2026 NSSF contributions are calculated on a wage of at least KHR 600,000 and at most KHR 1,500,000 (Joint Prakas 234/26), for pension, work-injury and health-care schemes
facts.q: Under Joint Prakas 234, the minimum and maximum contributable wages are now set at KHR 600,000 (approximately USD 150) and KHR 1,500,000 (approximately USD 375), respectively.

facts.c: NSSF's notification of 28 October 2026 applies the new thresholds from November 2026
facts.q: requiring the new thresholds to apply from November 2026 instead.

facts.c: Entering Cambodia clandestinely, by fraud or other illegal means: 3 to 6 months' jail, then expulsion
facts.q: shall be subjected to imprisonment for three to six months prior to his being expulsed out of the country.

facts.c: Altering, faking, lending or using under another name a residence card, labour card or labour contract, or a fake application for them: 5 to 15 years' jail, for accomplices too
facts.q: Anyone who scratches, erases, makes carbon copy, fakes, lends, or writes false name on the resident card, labor/working card, labor/employment contract, or uses those documents with a name different than his own, or files a fake application for these above documents, shall be subjected to imprisonment for a term of five (5) to fifteen (15) years.

facts.c: The Interior Minister can expel any foreigner working without a labour card
facts.q: c. working in the Kingdom of Cambodia without a labor/working card.

facts.c: An expulsion decision takes effect on signature; the person may complain to a court within 2 months
facts.q: Decision for the expulsion must be carried out immediately from the date of signature of the Minister of Interior. The concerned person shall have rights to file complaint to the court within a period of two (2) months.

facts.c: Expulsion is carried out within 7 days unless a court suspends it
facts.q: The expulsion shall be carried out within 7 days, after an official decision is made by the Minister of Interior; except when there is a court decision ordering the instant suspension of such implementation.

facts.c: Breaches of residence-card rules (such as an unrenewed card) are fined 50,000 to 1,000,000 riels, 1,000,001 to 2,000,000 for repeats
facts.q: Shall be subjected to fines from 50,000 to 1,000,000 Riels, for those foreigners who breached the provisions of Articles 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 and 23 of this Law.

facts.c: Expulsion can be added to any penalty under the Immigration Law
facts.q: there shall be respectively additional other sub-punishments including the expulsion from the territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

facts.c: Labour inspectors may fine an employer KHR 12.6 million (about USD 3,150) per foreign worker without a work permit (Guideline 517, 2023), up to KHR 63 million for five or more, tripled for repeats
facts.q: being KHR12.6 million (approximately USD 3,150) per foreign employee.

facts.c: The Immigration Law allows up to three months' jail and/or deportation for the foreign workers concerned
facts.q: Chapters 5 and 6 of the Law on Immigration provide for a term of imprisonment of up to three months and/or deportation orders for the foreign employees concerned.

facts.c: Employers had to apply for 2025 work permits by 31 March 2025
facts.q: The deadline to apply for 2025 foreign employee work permits from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (“MLVT”), being 31 March 2025, is fast approaching.

facts.c: In May 2026 Cambodia waived overstay fines for 602 Nepalis after embassy requests; Cambodia's new provisions allow arrest, fine and jail for foreigners who fail to leave within one month
facts.q: Cambodia’s new legal provisions allow authorities to arrest, fine and imprison foreign nationals who fail to leave the country within one month.

facts.c: Cambodia waived visa overstay fines for 602 Nepalis after the Nepali embassy's request
facts.q: The Cambodian government has waived visa overstay fines for 602 Nepali nationals who remained in the country after their visas expired, following diplomatic efforts by the Nepali Embassy in Bangkok.

facts.c: In October 2026 a group said over 1,800 Bangladeshis were stranded and urged their return before a visa-overstay fine waiver expired on 31 October
facts.q: urges the government to bring them back home on special flights before a visa-overstay fine waiver expires on Oct 31.

facts.c: Many stranded Bangladeshis had travelled with valid passports, visas and government clearances before being coerced into scam compounds
facts.q: many had travelled with valid passports, visas, and government clearances but were later coerced into illegal activities at online scam compounds

facts.c: The Law on Combating Online Scams was promulgated on 6 April 2026
facts.q: On April 6, 2026, the Royal Government of Cambodia promulgated a Royal Decree announcing the Law on Combating Online Scams.

facts.c: Committing a technology-enabled scam: 2 to 5 years' jail and KHR 200 to 500 million fine; with an organised group or many victims, 5 to 10 years and KHR 500 million to 1 billion
facts.q: Offenders are subject to 2 to 5 years of imprisonment and fines ranging from KHR200 million to KHR500 million.

facts.c: Scam offences by an organised group or with multiple victims: 5 to 10 years and KHR 500 million to 1 billion
facts.q: Where the offense involves an organized group or multiple victims, penalties increase to 5 to 10 years of imprisonment and fines ranging from KHR500 million to KHR1 billion.

facts.c: Recruiting or training others for scams: 2 to 5 years' jail; 5 to 10 years if the recruiter knowingly recruits trafficking victims or uses violence or detention
facts.q: Anyone who recruits or trains others to participate in technology-enabled scams will be subject to 2 to 5 years of imprisonment and a fine ranging from KHR200 million to KHR500 million.

facts.c: Collecting or using identity cards, passports or personal data to facilitate scams: 1 to 3 years and KHR 100 to 300 million
facts.q: The unlawful collection or use of identity cards, passports, or other personal information documents for the purpose of facilitating online scams is punishable by 1 to 3 years of imprisonment and a fine ranging from KHR100 million to KHR300 million.

facts.c: Courts can also confiscate assets and close bank accounts used in scams
facts.q: the court may impose additional measures, including confiscation of assets, seizure of property used in the commission of offenses, and closure of bank accounts or online platforms involved in scams.

facts.c: Scam convictions bring 2 to 5 years and fines up to USD 125,000
facts.q: The law lays out punishments of two to five ‌years in prison and fines of up to $125,000 for those convicted of online scams.

facts.c: Keeping, transporting or trafficking drugs: 2 to 5 years' jail and up to 10 million riels fine; larger quantities bring 5 to 30 years or life
facts.q: Unlawful keeping, transporting, or trafficking of narcotic substances as listed in Table I and Table II shall be punishable by imprisonment from 2 (two) years to 5 (five) years.

facts.c: Trafficking 240 grams or more of methamphetamine, amphetamine or ecstasy (or 80 grams of heroin) brings 20 to 30 years or life
facts.q: Shall be punishable by imprisonment from 20 (twenty) years to 30 (thirty) years or by life imprisonment

facts.c: The life-sentence tier covers 240 grams or more of amphetamine, methamphetamine or ecstasy
facts.q: 4) Amphetamine, methamphetamine or ecstasy with a pure quantity from 240 (two hundred and forty) grams;

facts.c: Using drugs: 1 to 6 months' jail and a 100,000 to 1,000,000 riel fine; repeat use 6 months to 1 year
facts.q: shall be punishable by imprisonment from 1 (one) month to 6 (six) months and may be held liable by a fine from 100,000 (one hundred thousand) Riels to 1,000,000 (one million) Riels.

facts.c: Under Prakas 073/25 (4 March 2025) a worker can complain to MLVT's Labour Dispute Department or the provincial or capital Department of Labour
facts.q: Any party to an individual labor dispute can file a complaint with the Labor Dispute Department of the MLVT or the Department of Labor at the capital or provincial level.

facts.c: The joint conciliation meeting must be within three weeks of the complaint
facts.q: which must be held within three weeks of the complaint being received.

facts.c: A claimant who misses the meeting or doesn't sign the minutes without reasonable excuse loses the complaint; an absent employer is deemed guilty as claimed
facts.q: If the claimant fails to attend the meeting or sign the minutes without a reasonable excuse, the complaint is void.

facts.c: If the respondent fails to attend without reasonable excuse, conciliation fails and the respondent is deemed guilty as claimed
facts.q: If the respondent fails to attend the meeting without a reasonable excuse, the conciliation is unsuccessful, and the respondent is deemed guilty as claimed.

facts.c: A claimant who fails to give required information within the deadline (plus three working days) has the complaint voided
facts.q: If the claimant fails to provide required information within the specified deadline (or within three working days thereafter without reasonable excuse), the complaint is deemed void.

facts.c: If conciliation fails, both sides can jointly ask MLVT for a second attempt within two working days
facts.q: If conciliation fails, the parties may jointly request further reconciliation by the MLVT within two working days.

facts.c: During conciliation either party can ask for referral to the Arbitration Council; the minister refers it within three working days
facts.q: During the conciliation, either party may request referral of the matter to the Arbitration Council

facts.c: The Arbitration Council is an independent national body set up in 2003 with quasi-judicial powers under the Labour Law to resolve collective labour disputes
facts.q: The Arbitration Council is an independent, national institution with quasi-judicial authority derived from the Labour Law of Cambodia.

facts.c: The family of a worker who dies abroad gets Tk 3 lakh from the Welfare Board, if the worker had BMET clearance or Board membership
facts.q: বিদেশে মৃত্যুবরণ করলে মৃত প্রবাসী কর্মীর পরিবার ওয়েজ আর্নার্স কল্যাণ বোর্ড হতে ৩.০০ (তিন) লক্ষ টাকা আর্থিক অনুদান পাবে। সেক্ষেত্রে প্রবাসী কর্মীর বহির্গমন ছাড়পত্র কিংবা বোর্ডের মেম্বারশীপ থাকতে হবে।

facts.c: The grant is paid only if the worker dies in the country for which BMET clearance was issued
facts.q: বহির্গমন ছাড়পত্র গ্রহণপূর্বক প্রবাসী কর্মী যে দেশে গমন করবেন কেবল সে দেশে মৃত্যুবরণ করলে মৃত কর্মীর পরিবারকে আর্থিক অনুদান প্রদান করা হবে

facts.c: If the body is buried abroad, the family must apply within one year of the death to the Board's Director General or through the district expatriate welfare centre
facts.q: মৃত কর্মীর লাশ বিদেশে স্থানীয়ভাবে দাফন করা হলে কর্মীর মৃত্যুর ০1 (এক) বছরের মধ্যে মৃতের পরিবারকে ওয়েজ আর্নার্স কল্যাণ বোর্ডের মহাপরিচালক বরাবর অথবা সংশ্লিষ্ট জেলা প্রবাসী কল্যাণ সেন্টারের মাধ্যমে আবেদন করতে হবে

facts.c: If the family received the Tk 35,000 cheque at the airport, no separate application for the grant is needed
facts.q: বিদেশে মৃত কর্মীর লাশ দেশে আসার পর বিমানবন্দর হতে মৃতের পরিবার ৩৫,০০০/- (পঁয়ত্রিশ হাজার) টাকার চেক গ্রহণ করলে আর্থিক অনুদানের জন্য আবেদন করার প্রয়োজন হবে না

facts.c: The grant goes to spouse, children and parents; to siblings only if the worker was unmarried and the parents are dead
facts.q: মৃত প্রবাসী কর্মীর স্ত্রী/স্বামী, সন্তান এবং পিতা ও মাতার মধ্যে সীমাবদ্ধ থাকবে।

facts.c: When a body arrives, the airport welfare desk gives the family a Tk 35,000 cheque for transport and burial
facts.q: মৃত সকল প্রবাসী কর্মীর লাশ দেশে আসার পর মৃতের পরিবারকে বিমানবন্দর হতে লাশ পরিবহন ও দাফন খরচ বাবদ ৩৫,০০০/- (পঁয়ত্রিশ হাজার) টাকার চেক প্রদান করা হবে।
